 St. Louis Streets Department prepares for winter
 BY 
 John Gerding
 St. Louis 
 PUBLISHED 1:00 PM CT Nov. 05, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 1:00 PM CST Nov. 05, 2026 
 SHARE 
 ST. LOUIS—The City of Saint Louis Streets Department is ordering salt and materials as it prepares for winter but officials are excited about the new snow route map system.
 Last winter season the department remapped the snow routes and was proceeding to digitize them, now those are complete and that’s great news for inquisitive residents.
 “The mayor wanted a more modernized system so that the residents could be able to track where we've been, what we've done, what's open and what we're currently operating on,” said James Jackson, Director of Street Department. “This system will give us the ability to do that and provide it to the residents publicly—we also wanted to ensure that all of our equipment had AVL tracking on them, that is in the process of being completed right now.”
 While the top three priorities for clearing crews remain the same —primary roadways, secondary roadways, followed by hills and problem areas— residential streets have been added as the fourth priority.
 “Those areas will be treated in those instances where we have two or more inches of precipitation, with a forecast of continuous precipitation and lower temperatures,” said Jackson.
 After precipitation ends, the streets department intends on having major roads cleared within 24 to 48 hours and residential streets by 72 hours. Last year, crews treated nearly 41,000 miles, while spreading 264,500 gallons of brine and 8,500 tons of salt.
 Mayor Spencer reiterated the city made numerous changes to how it prepared and addressed inclement conditions, including the Winter Weather Unified Command and the city’s Code Blue protocol.
 “We could not do this without the many, many, many people,” praised Spencer. “One of the biggest lessons learned was that the coordination was key and it was very effective.”
